text:
Alice Chen: Hey team — hit a bunch of 429s in production last night around 03:10 AM local. Console shows our monthly token balance at 0. We changed plan mid-cycle (upgraded to Pro) last week and also added two seats. Do monthly credits always reset at a fixed UTC midnight, or is our anchor tied to the subscription start date? Is there any way to get a temporary refill while we wait for the next cycle?

usage-bot: [automated] org=acme-ai usage snapshot: tokens_this_month=2,042,103 tokens_remaining=0 next_reset=1710556800 (UTC)

Jamal (Support): Sorry about the outage, Alice — totally understand the urgency. Quick answers up front:
1) Monthly quota resets at your billing anchor (the day/time your subscription started) at 00:00 UTC on that anchor day. It is not automatically shifted by changing plan mid-cycle.
2) Upgrading a plan applies additional quota immediately as an additive pro-rata credit (you should have seen an increase in tokens_balance when you upgraded). It does not move your monthly reset earlier.
3) We can issue a temporary top-up while billing reviews the pro-rata. To do that we need: org id, invoice/billing email, and a short justification (e.g., production outage).

Can you paste your org id or the account email? Also please include one full failing request (curl) with response headers if available — that helps confirm it’s a quota 429 vs auth/permission issue.

Alice Chen: org id is org_01G6FJ3LZ4Z9A9X2 billing email billing@acme.ai. Here’s one of the failing requests (sanitized):
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-large-2","prompt":"summarize...","max_tokens":1024}'
```
Response headers I captured: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 120
X-RW-Remaining-Tokens: 0
X-RW-Rate-Limit-Limit: 400000
X-RW-Rate-Limit-Window: 2592000
Content-Type: application/json
```
Response body shows the usual rate-limit error JSON.

Jamal (Support): Thanks — that header set is exactly a quota-exhaustion 429. The Retry-After is server recommended backoff (in seconds). We’ll loop in billing for a temporary top-up. @Marta can you advise on pro-rata/top-up?

Marta (Billing): Thanks @Jamal and @Alice. I see the upgrade on 1710000000 (mid-cycle). Upgrades add a pro-rated token credit immediately, but do not change the monthly reset anchor (your next_reset timestamp in usage-bot is correct). I can provision a one-time emergency top-up of tokens (we usually do +200k tokens for production incidents) — I need an approval note from the org owner or the billing contact to proceed. If you prefer, we can also do an invoice adjustment so future months reflect the change.

Alice Chen: We’d appreciate the emergency top-up. I’m copying our CFO in for approval. Quick Q: will future upgrades ever move the reset date? Because teams expect it to align with calendar months.

Ravi (Infra): Adding a bit of technical detail so you know what happened. Your account uses a token-bucket quota model:
- bucket_size = monthly_quota (refilled once per cycle at the anchor)
- refill occurs at anchor 00:00 UTC
- we allow a short-term burst window for some plans (hosted standard plans get a tiny in-flight grace for 1–2 requests to finish; Dedicated customers can configure burst policies).
In your case, the bucket reached 0, so subsequent requests were rejected with 429 and Retry-After showing estimated seconds until the bucket will accept more tokens. The X-RW-Rate-Limit-Window header indicates the configured cycle window (in seconds).

If you want to reproduce locally to see the headers:
```
# quick repro (sanitized) - run until you get a 429
for i in $(seq 1 2000); do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{redirect_url}\n" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-small","prompt":"x","max_tokens":128}' \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions || break
  sleep 0.05
done
```
Capture headers with `-i` to see Retry-After and X-RW-Remaining-Tokens. For a deterministic reproduce on a test org, set a low monthly quota in the console and run the loop.

Jamal (Support): Practical guidance while billing processes the top-up:
- Implement exponential backoff honoring Retry-After (start 500ms -> 2s -> 5s) and surfacing a user-friendly message in your app.
- Respect X-RW-Remaining-Tokens to show a real-time quota banner to product teams.
- Consider request batching and reducing max_tokens where possible to stretch the remaining quota.

Alice Chen: Thanks. Two more things: 1) We saw a short period where a few requests after the bucket hit 0 still returned 200 and completed — is that expected? 2) What is the paid-topup turnaround time?

Ravi (Infra): 1) Those successful post-zero requests were probably in-flight before the quota check completed; there's a small race window (a few hundred milliseconds) where in-flight requests are allowed to finish — not guaranteed and not something to rely on.
2) For emergency top-ups requested via support + billing approval we typically provision within 1–2 business hours. If you require immediate restoration, request an emergency top-up and mark the ticket "production outage"; include the org billing contact for authorization.

Marta (Billing): I’ve created a billing ticket and requested approval. Once approved we’ll add a one-time +200000 tokens and confirm in this thread. Please confirm the org owner email on the ticket is billing@acme.ai.

Alice Chen: Confirmed. Thank you — we’ve also implemented the Retry-After backoff in the client as a short-term mitigation.

usage-bot: [automated] billing.topup.request id=tb_9f3 created_by=Jamal status=pending

Marta (Billing): Approved — I provisioned +200000 tokens to org_01G6FJ3LZ4Z9A9X2. New usage-balance=200,000 tokens. This is a one-time emergency credit; monthly anchor unchanged.

Alice Chen: Received the greenlight; traffic resumed and errors dropped to zero. Really appreciate the quick help, @Jamal, @Marta, @Ravi :thumbsup:

Jamal (Support): Great — closing the loop. For future planning: if your traffic is bursty near month-end consider purchasing Dedicated / Reserved capacity or increasing monthly quota to avoid these sharp 429 cliffs. If you want, we can schedule a brief call to review usage patterns and recommendations.

Alice Chen: Yes please — can you send a calendar invite?

Jamal (Support): Will do. Follow-up ticket created: SUP-98012.
